proof:
Source: the parent proof's step 2e (Borel, finite measure) and step 3 (blow-up of an embedded C¹ piece), with details filled in.

Notation. ℝⁿ = Rn n, ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ, Hⁿ = μHE[n] (on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ = volume). B := B°_r(c) (open ball), N := G(B), B_s(y) closed balls. η_{x,λ}(y) := λ^(−1)(y − x) = Chapter03.blowUpMap x λ y. C_c denotes the compactly supported continuous f : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ. JG(b') := areaJacobianAt G b' = normDet(DG(b')) ≥ 0, a continuous function of b' (SimonGMT Chapter02.continuous_normDet composed with the continuous map DG). Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x P means: finrank P = n and ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N)} f dHⁿ → ∫_P f dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c.

Proof.
0. If r ≤ 0 then B = ∅, N = ∅, and all three claims are trivial; assume r > 0. The lower bound σ|b₁ − b₂| ≤ |G(b₁) − G(b₂)| on B with σ > 0 shows that G is injective on B.
1. Finite measure. DG is continuous, hence bounded by some Λ on the compact closed ball B_r(c). By the mean value inequality G is Λ-Lipschitz on the convex set B. Therefore Hⁿ(N) ≤ Λⁿ·Hⁿ(B) = Λⁿ·Lⁿ(B) < ∞ (SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn; Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ). This is (ii).
2. Borel. B is Borel and G is continuous and injective on B, so N = G(B) is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn). (Alternatively, B is σ-compact, hence so is N.) This is (i).
3. Fix b ∈ B and put x := G(b), L := DG(b), P := L(ℝⁿ) = LinearMap.range L. Since L is injective, finrank P = finrank ℝⁿ = n (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj). Fix f ∈ C_c and R > 0 with f = 0 outside B_R(0), and let M_f := sup|f|.
4. Rescaled parametrization (parent 3a). For λ > 0 let B^λ := {z ∈ ℝⁿ : b + λz ∈ B} (an open set) and Γ_λ(z) := λ^(−1)(G(b + λz) − x). Γ_λ is C¹ with DΓ_λ(z) = DG(b + λz), which is injective for z ∈ B^λ; Γ_λ is injective on B^λ (G is injective on B); and Γ_λ(B^λ) = η_{x,λ}(N), because η_{x,λ}(G(b')) = Γ_λ((b' − b)/λ).
5. Area formula (parent 3b). SimonGMT Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative, applied to Γ_λ on the Borel set B^λ (Γ_λ is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B^λ and injective on B^λ), gives, using areaJacobianAt Γ_λ z = normDet(DG(b + λz)) = JG(b + λz) and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ:
 ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{B^λ} JG(b + λz) f(Γ_λ(z)) dz = ∫_{ℝⁿ} F_λ(z) dz, where F_λ := 1_{B^λ}·JG(b + λ·)·(f ∘ Γ_λ).
 F_λ is measurable (continuous on the open set B^λ and zero outside it).
6. Uniform support and bound (parent 3c). If F_λ(z) ≠ 0 then z ∈ B^λ and |Γ_λ(z)| ≤ R, i.e. |G(b + λz) − G(b)| ≤ λR; the lower bound (both b and b + λz lie in B) gives σλ|z| ≤ λR, so |z| ≤ R/σ. With J_max := the maximum of the continuous function JG over the compact set B_r(c), we get |F_λ| ≤ M_f·J_max·1_{B_{R/σ}(0)} for every λ > 0: an integrable bound independent of λ.
7. Pointwise convergence (parent 3d). Fix z ∈ ℝⁿ. Since B is open and b ∈ B, b + λz ∈ B for all small λ > 0, so 1_{B^λ}(z) → 1. By differentiability of G at b, Γ_λ(z) = (G(b + λz) − G(b))/λ → Lz, hence f(Γ_λ(z)) → f(Lz) (f is continuous). By continuity of JG, JG(b + λz) → JG(b) =: J_L. Thus F_λ(z) → J_L·f(Lz).
8. Dominated convergence (parent 3e). The filter of λ → 0+ (𝓝[>] 0) is countably generated, so tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence yields ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N)} f dHⁿ → J_L ∫_{ℝⁿ} f(Lz) dz.
9. Linear area formula. L is injective, so L is measure preserving from J_L·(Hⁿ on ℝⁿ) to Hⁿ⌞P (SimonGMT Chapter02.measurePreserving_linearMap_normDet_smul, with normDet L = J_L). Hence ∫_P f dHⁿ = J_L ∫_{ℝⁿ} f(Lz) dz. Together with finrank P = n (step 3) this is exactly Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N (G b) (LinearMap.range (DG(b))), which is (iii). ∎
key_steps: Trivial if r ≤ 0; G injective on B by the lower bound
G Lipschitz on B (bounded continuous derivative) gives Hⁿ(N) < ∞; Lusin–Souslin gives N Borel
Rescaled parametrization Γ_λ of η_{G(b),λ}(N) on B^λ with DΓ_λ(z) = DG(b + λz)
Area formula: ∫_{η(N)} f = ∫ 1_{B^λ}(z) JG(b + λz) f(Γ_λ z) dz
Uniform support in B_{R/σ}(0) from the lower bound and a λ-independent bound; pointwise limit J_L f(Lz)
Dominated convergence and the linear area formula identify the limit with ∫_P f dHⁿ
